originality.rationale: Statement-level comparison found neither a matching Fourier-zero criterion nor a dominating result for mixtures of two gamma rates with common arbitrary real shape. Evin et al. provide gamma-mixture models but investigate Bayesian inference; Gaunt treats multiplicative gamma products; John examines gamma Laplace zeros mainly at one common rate. The resulting explicit exceptional-weight spectrum, universal shape-two threshold, sharp relative margin and complete Wiener cyclicity criterion are not implied by the inspected results. Remaining priority risk, especially Gharib (1995) abstract-only, is disclosed; a negative search is not itself proof of priority.
residual_risks: Older or unindexed characteristic-function zero results for gamma mixtures may imply the statement, including alternate phase/complex-power formulations.
Gharib (1995) DOI:10.1017/S0004972700014842 full text unavailable; abstract-level comparison cannot settle priority.
The Wiener cyclicity corollary is standard given the Fourier-zero classification and is not an independent novelty claim.

value.rationale: Solves the natural question whether mixing two individually zero-free gamma Fourier transforms preserves nonvanishing/Wiener translate cyclicity. The universal all-rates shape-two protection, exact scale-ratio transition, isolated exceptional weight classification, and sharp uniform relative conditioning constant give a complete structural phase diagram for arbitrary real gamma shapes. Quantitative stability and translate completeness make the exact criterion useful; it is more than a trivial evaluation of a known transform.
